absent: Locking discipline and concurrency rules for mapping, allocation, release, quirk application, and base initialization.
Numeric values of extended shared and extended private base identifiers, trigger sensitivity masks, and hardware range boundaries.
Register layouts and bit definitions beyond the sampled type and identification registers.
Behavior of per CPU and fast end of interrupt dispatch routines and of mask, unmask, completion, affinity, retrigger, and state callbacks.
Power management, suspend resume, and multiprocessor bringup contracts beyond the named setup calls.
Message based interrupt, virtualization, and secondary message controller initialization contracts.

findings.text: Two controller descriptors share one model name and a largely common capability set covering masking, completion, trigger programming, affinity, retrigger, state access, non maskable lifecycle, and inter processor signalling, with flags requiring masked type updates, skipped wake handling, and suspend masking. One uses a unified completion path. The companion uses a split completion path with distinct mask and completion behavior and adds virtual CPU affinity control. Selection between them follows platform split deactivate support.

Hardware identifiers are classified into per CPU families and shared families. Per CPU families are marked as per CPU device interrupts and bound to a per CPU dispatch routine. Shared families are bound to a fast end of interrupt dispatch routine. The shared wired families are additionally marked probeable and constrained to a single target. Every successful mapping records a requirement to enforce interrupt context in order to preserve acknowledgement ordering against software retrigger.

Mapping rejects unknown hardware ranges and rejects the message based family when the distributor does not advertise support for it. Both rejections use a permission style negative result. No other mapping failure modes appear in the observed fragments.

Translation from firmware description to hardware identifier supports three shapes. A single cell value below sixteen denotes a low software generated identifier with fixed rising edge sensitivity. A device tree description requires at least three cells where the first selects the family, the second carries an index, and the third carries sensitivity after masking. A firmware table interrupt chip description requires exactly two cells carrying a global identifier and sensitivity, rejecting low values as firmware bugs. Other shapes are rejected as invalid.

Device tree index handling uses fixed additions and warning thresholds. The shared family adds thirty two and warns beyond nine hundred eighty seven. The private family adds sixteen and warns beyond fifteen. The extended shared family adds a fixed extended base and warns beyond one thousand twenty three. The extended private family adds a fixed extended private base and warns beyond sixty three. The message based family passes its index through unchanged. The single cell shorthand covers values below sixteen.

Allocation performs one translation of the supplied firmware specifier and then maps a consecutive run of virtual interrupts onto consecutive hardware identifiers, stopping at the first mapping failure. Release walks the same run, clearing each dispatch routine and resetting the associated per interrupt domain data.

Domain selection first requires firmware node identity. An empty specifier matches only when the requested bus token equals the domain token. A non device tree specifier is accepted for the single domain case. Otherwise the specifier is translated and accepted only for the primary distributor domain, with translation failure treated as no match plus a one time warning.

Firmware affinity hints are honored only for device tree private families when a fourth cell carries a non zero partition reference. The reference is resolved against a partition table built elsewhere, with unresolvable references reported as missing entries. When no hint is present the set of all possible processors is reported. Successful queries are flagged as carrying valid affinity. Other families and non device tree descriptions report no affinity data.
Distributor domain behavior is published as a table of five operations covering firmware translation, allocation, release, domain selection, and firmware information query.

Platform errata handling is table driven. Entries match by compatible string, by distributor identification value under mask, or by boolean property. Each entry names a handler that records workaround state in global distributor data or enables a global capability branch and reports whether it applied. The table covers several named implementations, two steppings of one product sharing a handler, a coherence forcing property, and a machine gated insecure integration check.

One fabric erratum uses a chip number field covering bits forty five through forty four, a distributor alias offset of 0x1580000, and a system on chip identity of 0x036b0241. Activation requires at least three distinct chips observed across redistributor regions. Per chip alias windows use sixty four kilobyte mappings.

One erratum handler first validates system on chip identity, then derives a chip presence mask from redistributor physical addresses, aborts when fewer than three chips are present, otherwise creates per chip distributor alias mappings and enables a dedicated capability branch.

Non maskable support proceeds only when priority masking is active and a global forbid flag is clear. When enabled it logs the synchronization mode, enables a dedicated capability branch, and marks whichever controller descriptor is currently selected as supporting non maskable operation.

Base initialization captures firmware handle, distributor address and mapping, redistributor descriptors, count and stride, then samples distributor type state, applies the erratum table keyed by distributor identification, and conditionally samples extended type state unless a known reserved access workaround is active. It creates the wired tree domain, allocates per CPU redistributor state, and initializes virtual message capabilities unless a fabric erratum disables them. Allocation failure removes the domain and releases per CPU state. Success continues through token assignment, optional message setup, top level dispatch installation, property and priority and distributor and CPU setup, non maskable enablement, multiprocessor and power management setup, and a final branch between message based setup and a secondary message controller.

Device tree initialization maps the distributor window, validates distributor architecture, determines region count defaulting to one and stride defaulting to zero, maps each redistributor region, applies device tree quirks, initializes common bases, builds private partition state, and conditionally records virtualization information when split deactivation is active. Mapping or validation failures unwind previously acquired mappings and report a negative result.

Firmware table boot storage records distributor mapping, region descriptors, region count, single region mode, enabled count, maintenance interrupt number and mode, and virtual CPU base. Registration appends one region per call with a monotonic counter while preserving the current single region flag. Table parsing maps each advertised region, optionally forces non shareable coherence based on revision and entry flags, reserves the address range, and registers the mapping.

Private partition discovery returns silently when an optional child node is absent or empty. Otherwise it allocates one affinity record per child, records each child identity, parses each affinity list of processor references into a processor mask while warning and skipping malformed entries, and publishes the table and count globally. Virtualization information recording captures a maintenance interrupt and an address resource indexed after distributor and redistributor windows, copies virtualization capability flags, and publishes through a helper that is a no operation in the observed configuration.

Distributor version validation samples a product identification register under an architecture mask and accepts only the two major architecture generations covered by this driver, rejecting anything else as absent hardware.

The included headers publish small inline utilities usable by other compilation units for context enforcement marking, probe marking, descriptor data access, dispatch routine assignment, tree domain creation, top level dispatch installation, and virtualization information publication.

Several defenses guard against platform and firmware defects. Address reservation conflicts produce a firmware bug warning without failing. One hardware family skips a second type register read because reserved accesses fault. Out of range indices produce one time warnings but continue with computed identifiers. Unspecified sensitivity and failed domain selection produce warnings. Illegal low global identifiers in firmware table translation are rejected with an error.
In the observed headers the top level dispatch installer discards its argument and warns, indicating a fallback or disabled configuration rather than a functional installation path.
